item.title: Creating objects and assignment
item.description:
Creating objects

TrustLang uses several operators to create objects:

item.title: Operators
item.description:
Arithmetic operators

The arithmetic operators of TrustLang are applicable to numeric types and to assignment forms. Each binary operator has a paired analog op=, which performs the operation and assigns the result to the left operand (a += 1;):

Operator Action
+ / += addition
- / -= subtraction
* / *= multiplication (also applicable for repeating strings)
/ / /= division (the result is a floating-point number)
// / //= integer division rounded toward the smaller value (as in Python)
% / %= remainder of integer division

There is no separate exponentiation operator (the power is computed by a function/repeated multiplication). Arithmetic of rational numbers and :BigInteger is a separate strict branch: mixing with floating-point numbers requires an explicit conversion (see Numbers and tensors).

item.title: Conditions and loops
item.description: In TrustLang there is no if keyword: a condition is checked by a construct that in meaning corresponds to the mathematical “follows” — two dashes and an angle bracket -->. The notation is easily combined into chains for checking several conditions of the “else if” kind. item.title: Context manager (with)
item.description:
The single statement for capturing a reference and synchronizing access to an object (*ref, *ref(...)) is executed for one action. Capturing a reference/synchronization object is a relatively slow operation, so performing it for each action is inefficient. The context manager (with) captures several references/objects at once and performs a group of actions under a common lock, and also serves for automatic resource release (RAII) when leaving the block.

In the base syntax — the operator **( ... ); in DSL it corresponds to the macro @with (see Keyword syntax (DSL)). Comparison of the notation forms using the example of capturing-locking a reference:

item.title: Expressions and statements
item.description:
In TrustLang any construct is an expression and returns a value, so it can be nested inside other expressions. Statements are separated by a semicolon ;; a group of statements is enclosed in a code block { ... }. The basic rules of blocks and expressions are described in Syntax.

Handling of emergencies and guarantees of resource release are related to the Memory model, and typing operators — to the Type system.

item.title: Return, interrupts and error handling
item.description:
A sequence of commands (a code block) can be interrupted at any point by special interrupt statements. TrustLang uses two kinds of interrupts, which in meaning correspond to their notation:

  • “positive” interrupt ++ — return of a value/through-flow (analog of return);
  • “negative” interrupt -- — error (analog of throw).

An interrupt can return a value: ++ 'String' ++ — return a string, -- err -- — “throw” an error (a rough analog of throw err). If no value is specified, the interrupt returns nothing (an empty value).
